OPEN DATA, EXPLAINED

A view of the grid.
With the details intact.

What does the map measure?

Renewable share is wind, solar, natural hydro, biomass, geothermal and other reported renewables divided by reported generation. Low-carbon share adds nuclear. Both exclude pumped-storage and battery discharge, whose original energy mix is unknown. Mixed waste and unspecified generation are counted in the denominator, not assumed renewable.

These are shares of domestic reported generation, not the electricity consumed in a country. Imports can change the consumption mix. Public-generation coverage varies by country, including how rooftop solar and industrial self-generation are reported.

Real readings, independent clocks

The site collects data every 30 minutes using GitHub Actions. The schedule is best effort; providers may publish with longer delays. Generation, border flows, prices and Danish CO₂ retain their own timestamps. An old or incomplete reading is labelled, and missing values are never turned into zero.

Historical map positions show the last reading within each UTC hour. Detailed charts retain the source intervals; gaps are not interpolated. All displayed times are UTC, avoiding ambiguity when clocks change.

Cross-border flows

Physical exchanges come from Energy-Charts. Positive net exchange means imports exceed exports. Arrows show a selected country’s reported exchanges; countries may report different values at different times. This is not a transmission-line map, and the app does not infer the carbon intensity of imports from these flows.

Denmark’s CO₂ figures

Energinet’s CO2Emis feed estimates operational CO₂ intensity of electricity consumption for DK1 and DK2, accounting for exchange. These preliminary readings can contain uncorrected errors. They are not lifecycle CO₂-equivalent estimates and should not be compared directly with Electricity Maps’ carbon intensity. No European consumption-carbon estimate is presented.

Great Belt exchange is included when estimating each Danish area’s demand. Bornholm–Sweden exchange is already included in the Sweden field and is not counted twice.

Prices are wholesale, not household bills

Prices are day-ahead prices in EUR/MWh, excluding retail charges and taxes. Multiple bidding zones are shown separately. Only Energy-Charts price zones explicitly licensed for public reuse under CC BY 4.0 are included. Missing price coverage does not mean electricity is free.
